analysis:
Documentation-only PR touching docs/architecture/inference.md and docs/developer/test.md. The supplied head_text units (inference.md lines 2037-2600) are unchanged surrounding MiMo/Flint/Qwen4 text. The actual changes are visible only in the file_changes patch excerpt. Date bumps appear in both files. In inference.md, the Nemotron Super encoded-body bound is described as moving from 8 MiB to 40 MiB at head lines 128-132 and 542-544. The 40 MiB bound is justified as one part at the shared 25 MiB inline-media cap as base64. The over-limit error is described as `media_too_large` (previously the invalid-media 400). The doc says the video-over-context case remains a 400 and the charge-exceeds-budget case remains a 503. In test.md, a new Nemotron OpenRouter video test description was added at lines 1073-1077.

Security relevance: this is a documented increase of the request-body ceiling, affecting availability and memory under the existing TB-002 and TB-007 trust boundaries with adversarial consumers. The doc states that the media memory reservation is taken from the shared budget before decoding and refused with 503 when it does not fit. That means the decode allowance, and not the body size, still gates memory. The code change itself is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify that the 40 MiB limit is enforced before allocation or that the memory-admission charge still applies to the larger encoded body. This should be confirmed in the source pass for NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes and the admission path.

No security controls are weakened by these documentation edits, and nothing here invalidates the threat model. No findings. needs_deeper_review is set because the implementation is outside the supplied evidence and the larger body cap is not checked against code.
